answer_text:
Since \(\log\) is strictly increasing, minimizing

\[
f(x)=\log\left(\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-x_i}\right)
\]

is equivalent to minimizing

\[
g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-x_i}.
\]

The function \(\phi(t)=e^{-t}\) is convex because \(\phi''(t)=e^{-t}>0\). By Jensen’s inequality,

\[
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-x_i}
\ge
e^{-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}.
\]

Using the constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1\), we get

\[
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-x_i}
\ge
e^{-1/n}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{i=1}^n e^{-x_i}
\ge
n e^{-1/n},
\]

and therefore

\[
f(x)\ge \log\left(n e^{-1/n}\right)=\log n-\frac{1}{n}.
\]

Equality in Jensen’s inequality holds if and only if all \(x_i\) are equal. Since \(\sum_i x_i=1\), this gives

\[
x_i=\frac{1}{n}\qquad \text{for all } i.
\]

This point satisfies the bounds \(0\le x_i\le 1\) for every \(n\ge 1\). Hence it is the unique minimizer.

\[
\boxed{x_i=\frac{1}{n}\ \text{ for all } i=1,\dots,n}
\]
